name: Granite 3.3 8B Instruct
definition: Granite 3.3 8B Instruct is a dense enterprise-oriented instruction and reasoning model developed by IBM in the Granite 3.3 family. It has 8B parameters, supports 128K tokens of context, accepts Text / code and produces Text / code. Its primary role is enterprise assistants, RAG, structured extraction, reasoning, code and function calling.

architecture.model_type: dense enterprise-oriented instruction and reasoning model
details: Structured reasoning with <think> and <response> style separation
Designed for multilingual enterprise and coding tasks

training.summary: IBM says the model is trained on a carefully balanced mix of permissively licensed data and curated synthetic tasks, then fine-tuned for reasoning and instruction following. The model card emphasizes generic assistant quality as well as mathematics, coding and structured enterprise tasks.

deployments.notes: Granite models are compatible with standard transformer-serving stacks.
Granite is part of IBM’s enterprise model ecosystem.

hardware.summary: An 8B dense model is practical on a single modern GPU and on CPU/unified-memory systems under quantization. 128K context can become the dominant memory consumer for long sessions, so weight size alone is not sufficient sizing.

limitations: 128K context may require much more memory than short enterprise prompts.
Structured reasoning tags are a prompting/output convention, not guaranteed faithful internal reasoning.
Twelve listed languages have varying quality.
Enterprise deployments still need domain-specific retrieval, access control and evaluation.
